_note: The shared cross-domain vocabulary. An option `provides` these and `requires` these. Every `requires` must be `provides`-able by at least one option somewhere in the catalogue, or `eas lint` fails - an unsatisfiable requirement is a catalogue bug, not a run finding.

identity.subject-schema.desc: A canonical who/what subject schema exists and is emitted on every security-relevant action.

identity.pdp.central.desc: Authorisation decisions are made by an external, centrally governed policy decision point.

identity.workload.federated.desc: Workloads authenticate with short-lived federated credentials; no long-lived static secrets.

identity.privileged.jit.desc: Privileged access is just-in-time / just-enough, brokered and recorded.

identity.secrets.managed.desc: Secrets and certificates live in a managed store with an enforced rotation lifecycle.

identity.mtls.identity.desc: Workload identity is strong enough to underpin mTLS / SPIFFE-style peer authentication.

identity.federation.external.desc: External (partner/customer) IdP federation trust is inventoried and governed.

network.reach.control-plane.desc: Reachability exists from every workload to IdP / PDP / KMS control planes, in every environment.

network.private.only.desc: No public data path; all service-to-service connectivity is private.

network.egress.inspected.desc: Internet-bound traffic is decrypted and inspected at L7 before leaving.

network.egress.fqdn-allowlist.desc: Outbound is constrained to an explicit FQDN/URL allow-list, not IP ranges.

network.segmentation.micro.desc: East-west traffic is policed per service pair, not just at the perimeter.

network.dns.deterministic.desc: Name resolution is deterministic and intentional per environment; split-horizon behaviour is designed, not inherited.

network.ingress.waf.desc: Public ingress is fronted by a WAF with a managed rule posture.

network.flowlogs.desc: Flow logs are produced and shipped as a SecOps source.

network.residency.pinned.desc: Routing and every failover path stay inside the declared residency boundary.

data.classification.per-flow.desc: Every store and every flow carries a classification, not just every system.

data.key.customer-managed.desc: Encryption keys are customer-managed (CMK/BYOK) with a known blast radius per key.

data.key.hyok.desc: Keys are held outside the processing platform (HYOK / external key store).

data.residency.in-region.desc: Data at rest and in transit stays within the declared jurisdiction.

data.tokenised.desc: The maximum-sensitivity elements are tokenised or masked before they reach general-purpose stores.

data.dlp.egress.desc: Every egress path is covered by a data-loss control.

data.nonprod.synthetic.desc: Non-prod uses generated synthetic data; no production-derived records.

data.nonprod.masked.desc: Non-prod uses irreversibly masked production-derived data under a stated guarantee.

data.retention.policy.desc: Retention and disposal are defined per classification and enforced.

data.access.audited.desc: Data-plane access produces Type 1 audit events attributable to a subject.

integration.edge.authz.desc: Authorisation is verified at every trust-boundary edge, never inferred from network location.

integration.contract.governed.desc: Interface contracts and schemas are versioned and governed.

integration.async.idempotent.desc: Asynchronous paths are idempotent and handle replay and poison messages.

integration.gateway.managed.desc: External API exposure is via a managed gateway with a policy layer.

integration.thirdparty.registered.desc: Third-party integrations are registered with materiality / CTP assessment.

integration.per-edge-logging.desc: Every interface emits a log a detection can consume.

secops.log.type1.desc: A security/audit logging pipeline exists with regulatory retention.

secops.log.type2.desc: An operational/observability pipeline exists for health and performance.

secops.log.separated.desc: Type 1 and Type 2 are separated at ingestion - different retention, access and cost.

secops.detection.egress.desc: Detection content exists for egress and exfiltration paths.

secops.detection.identity.desc: Detection content exists for identity abuse and privilege escalation.

secops.nonprod.monitored.desc: Non-prod environments are monitored, not detection blind spots.

secops.soar.desc: Response is at least partly automated via playbooks.

secops.ir.runbook.desc: An incident-response runbook with evidence handling covers this scope.

platform.provenance.signed.desc: Build artefacts are signed and their provenance is verifiable.

platform.admission.control.desc: Only verified artefacts can be admitted to a runtime.

platform.iac.governed.desc: Infrastructure is declared as code and gated by policy with drift detection.

platform.runtime.protection.desc: Runtime behaviour is monitored and constrained on the workload itself.

platform.parity.pipeline.desc: The same pipeline builds every environment; RTL is not hand-crafted.

platform.workload.identity.desc: The platform can mint and attest workload identity.

resilience.multi-az.desc: The service survives the loss of one availability zone.

resilience.multi-region.desc: The service survives the loss of a region.

resilience.backup.tested.desc: Backups exist and restores are tested on a stated cadence.

resilience.capacity.headroom.desc: Provisioned capacity carries stated headroom above measured peak.

grc.control.mapping.desc: Applicable controls are mapped to requirements with a named evidence source.

grc.evidence.automated.desc: Evidence is produced by the pipeline, not assembled by hand at audit time.

grc.exception.register.desc: Exceptions and waivers are registered with an owner and an expiry.

grc.modelrisk.tiered.desc: Models/LLMs in scope are tiered and their scoring is decomposable and defensible.

grc.thirdparty.dora.desc: Third parties are assessed against DORA / CTP thresholds with exit plans.

env.parity.asserted.desc: What differs between environments is a recorded decision, not drift.

env.promotion.gated.desc: Promotion passes explicit gates that verify stated properties.

env.data.policy.desc: A per-environment data policy exists and is enforced.

env.rtl.representative.desc: RTL is representative enough to catch what Prod will hit.

_implies_note: A stronger position satisfies a weaker requirement. Fully synthetic non-prod satisfies a requirement for masked non-prod; multi-region satisfies multi-AZ. Without this the orchestrator raises false contradictions between two positions that agree.
